evals.prompt: I want to create a new case but I do not have an sdd.md yet
evals.expected_output: Skill shows the roadmap, asks the Listen opener once (bare request), designs the case by best assumption, and confirms it in ONE decision-first Case Review that is complete enough to approve without opening sdd.md
expectations: The case-management skill was triggered

Shows the high-level journey first: reads the request and makes the design calls, one review packet with every decision for confirmation, then build and validate without interruptions, pausing only before publishing
Does not expose internal Phase 0 through Phase 5 labels in the user-facing roadmap
Asks the Listen opener once, then fills every open field by best assumption — no per-dimension question walk about trigger, task types, exits, or SLAs

Presents ONE Case Review with the required sections: Case Snapshot, Primary Journey, Other Paths Considered, SLA and Escalations, Rules and Outcomes, Resources and Integrations, Decisions I Made, Review Flags, and Caller obligation when relevant
The Case Review names every stage and every task in the Primary Journey or Other Paths tables, with task type, activation mode, required/optional status, routing/exit behavior, and SLA context
The approval surface omits the data contract, variables, task inputs, task outputs, and duplicated stage/task detail cards; those technical details remain in sdd.md
SLA and Escalations has one row per meaningful scope, SLA, and status combination, including the target or condition, response, response target, interrupting behavior, and rationale
The confirmation includes a complete Decisions I Made table with a plain-language provenance per assumption
A manually triggered task is presented as optional adhoc worker-launched work without exposing schema mechanics
The confirmation carries the build continuation choice (build straight through vs pause at the build preview) so it is never asked mid-build
On a Build answer, sdd.md is written batched with the first build actions and mentioned in one line as a reference artifact — never presented for review

evals.prompt: Create a vendor onboarding case. I attached two process documents. It uses VendorRiskAgent, Salesforce Prod, and a Slack notification connector.
evals.expected_output: Skill starts the tenant chain only when the description names tenant-bound work, designs in parallel with it, joins it at confirmation time without waiting, and never pulls twice in the session
expectations: Does not touch the tenant at entry — the background login and registry chain starts only once the description names tenant-bound work (the agent, Salesforce, the Slack connector), in the same batch as other work
Reads all supplied documents in parallel while the chain resolves
Runs registry pull only after login succeeds and does not treat a failed pull as zero matches
Joins the chain at confirmation time: ONE parallel name-match lookup per named resource — no tasks describe, no case spec, no schema discovery in Phase 0
If the pull has not finished when the confirmation is ready, presents anyway with resolve-at-build on tenant-bound items — the confirmation is never delayed by the tenant
With four or more independent lookups pending, may fan them out to parallel read-only workers that never write artifacts or prompt the user

A single confident match is adopted silently and shown as a decision; multiple matches, cross-folder names, missing connections, and empty lookups become resolve-at-build decisions — never a Phase 0 question
Does not let tenant inventory add or rename business stages or tasks
On the Build answer, Phase 1 reuses this session's successful pull instead of re-pulling; its Rule 17 gate remains where ambiguity is decided

evals.prompt: Interview me, confirm your understanding, and generate the SDD only after I approve it
evals.expected_output: Skill designs in memory with no draft files, and because the user requested a final sign-off it shows the explicit approval prompt and writes sdd.md only after approval
expectations: Keeps the design in session memory — no sdd.draft.md or checkpoint files are written during the interview
Runs the finalization checks against the in-memory model before presenting the confirmation, fixing failures silently

Shows one Case Review with Case Snapshot, Primary Journey, Other Paths Considered, SLA and Escalations, Rules and Outcomes, Resources and Integrations, Review Flags, and a complete Decisions I Made table
Because the user explicitly asked to approve first, an explicit approval prompt follows the confirmation — no file is created before it
On correction, updates the model, re-runs affected checks, and re-shows only the changed rows
On approval, writes sdd.md and proceeds directly to Phase 1 without asking the user to review the SDD document

evals.prompt: Build me a complete employee-offboarding case end to end. I trust the design process — I don't need to review anything until it's ready to run.
evals.expected_output: Skill designs by best assumption, confirms once (capturing the straight-through choice), then writes sdd.md batched with the first build actions and runs Phase 1 through Phase 4 automatically, pausing next at the publish gate
expectations: The single Case Review carries the build continuation choice: build straight through vs pause at the build preview

The Case Review is complete enough to approve without opening sdd.md: it includes Case Snapshot, Primary Journey, Other Paths Considered, SLA and Escalations, Rules and Outcomes, Resources and Integrations, Decisions I Made, and Review Flags while keeping data and variable details in sdd.md
The confirmation's Decisions I Made table discloses every assumption with plain-language provenance
On the Build answer, the transition line is announced and sdd.md is written in the same batch as the first build actions — never as a standalone blocking turn
One line reports the design doc path as a reference artifact
No blocking prompt between the confirmation and Phase 4 validation on the straight-through path — the Phase 2 boundary prints the skeleton counts line and continues
The build proceeds from the in-memory model without re-reading the just-written sdd.md, and Phase 1 reuses this session's successful registry pull instead of re-pulling
Posts an expectation-setting line before long silent work and one-line business-language milestones during the build — no internal phase or mode names
Still stops at the publish gate — never bypassed — and never offers or runs a debug session
If any high review item exists, the Build option is relabeled build-despite with the count

evals.prompt: Create a claims-intake case for me. (Tenant login is currently broken in this environment.)

Continues the interview without blocking on tenant discovery
Keeps concrete intended resource names and marks only identity/folder fields unresolved with paired review items
Does not surface internal filenames, cache paths, or CLI mechanics in the notice

evals.prompt: Build a case from this requirements document: ./claim-settlement-requirements.md (a complete spec: 5 phases with per-phase SLA targets, 3 wrap-up outcomes, a 4-way adjuster decision, amount-tiered sign-off, anytime actions).

Asks at most one batched clarifying call, and only for genuine contradictions in the spec — everything the doc covers is assumed, not re-confirmed

The Case Review includes Case Snapshot, Primary Journey, Other Paths Considered, SLA and Escalations, Rules and Outcomes, Resources and Integrations, Review Flags, and a complete Decisions I Made table with plain-language provenance
The five phase SLA targets and their at-risk or breach responses appear as separate rows in SLA and Escalations, not mixed into task cards or variable details

evals.prompt: Design a claims intake case with me — I want to see the case take shape as we go

On the Build answer, sdd.md is written batched with the first build actions and reported in one line as a reference artifact
High-severity review items still require the explicit build-despite opt-in

evals.prompt: Design a supplier application case. Withdrawal can arrive from the supplier portal at any point. Each phase warns handlers at 70% of its SLA and, on breach, interrupts into an escalation lane that creates an operations-lead task and sends the supplier a delay note. The case has a 15-day SLA whose breach interrupts into a director-review lane before closure. In Supplier Setup, verify identity, then set the supplier record, then invite the supplier. Preserve why every stage kind, task type, activation/sequence, SLA, and routing choice was made in the SDD and implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: Skill models global withdrawal/SLA events as interrupting secondary-stage entries, preserves explicit sequential work with runs-sequentially, and carries durable design rationale into tasks.md
expectations: Withdrawal is one interrupting secondary stage entered by the supplier-portal wait-for-connector event; the skill does not repeat withdrawal tasks or exits on every primary stage

The 70% at-risk warning is an SLA escalation notification; phase/case breach work uses sla-status-change entry rules on interrupting secondary stages that reference the intended SLA rules (a breach references the SLA alone; only an at-risk rule also names an escalation)

The explicitly ordered Supplier Setup tasks each use runs-sequentially, are not emitted as parallel current-stage-entered tasks, and are laid out as consecutive single-task data.tasks sets rather than one parallel inner array
The SDD stores design rationale for stage kind/routing, task type/activation/sequencing, and SLA behavior instead of leaving the reasons only in chat
tasks.md preserves the SDD rationale on the matching stage, task, condition, and SLA T-entries
